nearbyCountiesFullText.nwsHeadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM SATURDAY TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY
nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 201726
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1226 PM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very mild with near record highs in the mid to upper 60s today and 
  Saturday.

- Rain return Sunday with 60-80% chances. Scattered light showers 
  likely at times with rainfall amounts up to 0.10".

- Seasonable next week with highs in the upper 30s to low 40s.

- Thanksgiving forecast: highs near 40 degrees with 20-30%
  chances for scattered rain/snow showers.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1226 PM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

Surface high pressure centered over the Appalachian Mountains 
continues to provide tranquil, dry weather for the next 48 hours or 
so. Our mild weather pattern persists. High temperatures have been 
15-20 degrees above normals and lows about 5-10 degrees above normal 
the past few days. With southerly low level flow and WAA, 
temperatures are expected to remain in the mid to upper 60s for 
highs today and Saturday. This is abnormal for this time of year, as 
daily records for today (November 20th) and Saturday (November 21st) 
are around 70 degrees! 

As high pressure gets pushed eastward Saturday due to influence from 
a trough over the Four Corners region, rain chances return on Sunday 
as a cold front approaches. A low pressure system will traverse the 
Upper Midwest, with a trailing attendant cold front sweeping through 
the Great Lakes. There are 60-80% chances for rain, however, 
the day will not be a washout. Scattered, light showers will 
move through the area at times on Sunday during the day. 
Rainfall amounts are expected to be light (up to 0.10") as 
showers outrun the better low level moisture and lift with the 
actual front. It will be breezy on Sunday with a tightening 
pressure gradient in the vicinity of the front; Wind gusts will 
be between 20-25 mph with a shift in direction from southwest to
northwest. With the rain chances primarily in the afternoon and
evening, there should be sufficient diurnal heating for 
temperatures to climb into the low to mid 60s for highs on 
Sunday, especially in NW Ohio.

Following the frontal passage, CAA and northerly flow ensues with 
temperatures moderating back towards seasonable levels with highs in 
the upper 30s to low 40s. As a high pressure system spills into the 
Great Lakes region from central Canada, the forecast is leaning 
cooler and dry for early into middle part of next week. The GFS and 
ECMWF are in solid agreement next week of 850 mb temps below 0C 
through the early part of next week. This should result in highs in 
the low 40s and lows in the mid to upper 20s for several days. Given 
that a strong El Nino is ongoing, a more active pattern may develop 
across the southeastern US with the jet stream keeping activity 
suppressed to the south. There is some indication in the long 
range guidance of a 'Miller A' type system developing mid to 
late next week, but a lot of uncertainty remains. It is 
plausible we get some scattered rain/snow showers at times by 
mid to late next week, but there are no real signs of winter 
yet. An early look at Thanksgiving has highs near 40 degrees 
with 20-30% chances for scattered rain/snow showers.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 1107 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

The western periphery of high pressure will keep VFR conditions
in place through the TAF cycle. Winds will generally remain 
light, generally less than 10 knots.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Air Quality Alert from 6 PM Saturday to 10 AM EST Sunday for 
     INZ005.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Johnson
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.summary: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms may occur this afternoon through tonight across parts of the northeast Florida Peninsula, with occasional damaging winds and perhaps a brief tornado possible.
spc.text:
SPC AC 201624

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1024 AM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

   Valid 201630Z - 211200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   COASTAL NORTHEAST FLORIDA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms may occur this afternoon
   through tonight across parts of the northeast Florida Peninsula,
   with occasional damaging winds and perhaps a brief tornado possible.

   ...Florida...
   A weak surface low analyzed along/near the FL Space Coast should
   attempt to develop inland/northward through tonight, with some
   guidance showing it reforming over the northeast Gulf by early
   Saturday morning. A continued flux of rich low-level moisture will
   persist to the north of this low across the northeast FL Peninsula,
   with modestly enhanced low-level flow (around 25-35 kt) noted on
   recent VWPs from KJAX. Ongoing cloudiness/precipitation will likely
   limit diurnal destabilization, with lapse rates aloft also forecast
   to remain poor. Still, weak instability is forecast to develop
   offshore and spread slightly inland very near the coast through
   tonight. Even with modest mid-level flow expected to limit
   deep-layer shear, veering/strengthening winds in the low levels
   should still support some updraft rotation/organization with cells
   offshore moving west-northwestward towards the coast. An occasional
   waterspout/brief tornado threat may exist with this activity, along
   with some risk for isolated strong to damaging winds. A focused
   Marginal Risk has been added to account for this scenario, although
   meager instability inland will likely limit any appreciable severe
   risk to along/very near the coast of the northeast FL Peninsula.

   ..Gleason/Weinman.. 11/20/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 201733

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1133 AM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM WESTERN
   NORTH TEXAS INTO WESTERN OKLAHOMA AND SOUTH-CENTRAL KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over the central and
   southern Plains Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A strong shortwave trough will impact the southern High Plains
   during the early evening into the overnight. A weak surface low will
   develop and move eastward through Oklahoma as this occurs. Modest
   moisture return ahead of the surface low and cold front across the
   central Plains/upper Mississippi Valley will allow for some
   destabilization to occur. However, temperatures are still expected
   to remain on the cool side. Another nebulous upper trough will exist
   across the Southeast into Florida and the Carolinas. A complex
   forecast is evident with one or more surface lows developing. The
   evolution/track of these features remains uncertain.

   ...Central/southern Plains...
   Mid to upper 50s F dewpoints advecting into Oklahoma and parts of
   Kansas appear plausible as southerly flow increases ahead of the
   trough to the west. The strongest forcing for ascent will eject into
   the southern High Plains and western Oklahoma after 00Z. Cloud cover
   and possible elevated convection earlier in the day will tend to
   keep buoyancy low (only around 500 J/kg MUCAPE expected). Shear will
   be strong enough to support at least marginally organized clusters
   with slightly greater cellular potential near the surface low along
   the TX Panhandle/OK border. Strong/damaging winds are expected to be
   the main concern. Should stronger cells develop, small to marginally
   severe hail would also be possible.

   ...Coastal Carolinas...
   The risk for isolated damaging winds or brief tornado remains highly
   conditional given the uncertain state of inland destabilization.
   Most guidance shows minimal intrusion of greater surface moisture,
   though the HRRR would suggest the warm sector may approach parts of
   southeast North Carolina early Sunday morning. Uncertainty remains
   too high for severe probabilities.

   ..Wendt.. 11/20/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.riskAtLaPorte: No thunderstorm or severe risk area
spc.summary: Scattered thunderstorms are possible over parts of the middle and lower Mississippi valley Sunday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 200829

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0229 AM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

   Valid 221200Z - 231200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered thunderstorms are possible over parts of the middle and
   lower Mississippi valley Sunday.

   ...Mid to Lower MS Valley...
   The upper trough and associated cold front over the southern Plains
   will move eastward into the middle and lower MS Valley and slowly
   weaken through Sunday. Continued southerly low-level flow will
   transport low 60s F surface dewpoints as far north as AR allowing
   for modest destabilization. Remnant thunderstorms are likely to be
   ongoing ahead of the cold front from the Midwest, south toward the
   Ozarks and Sabine River early Sunday morning. These may reinvigorate
   somewhat as they move into the gradually destabilizing air mass
   across AR and LA.

   Low 60s F surface dewpoints should allow for around 500 J/kg of
   MLCAPE from northern LA into southern AR, though lapse rates are
   expected to remain modest. Mid-level winds are also forecast to
   weaken somewhat through the day as the shortwave trough moves
   northeastward. Still, 20-30kt of deep-layer shear could support a
   few stronger clusters or transient supercells through Sunday
   afternoon, but confidence is not high. If a few stronger storms do
   form, isolated hail and damaging gusts would be possible, most
   likely across southern AR, northern LA and perhaps far western MS.
   Any convection should weaken overnight as the front moves eastward
   into a cooler and drier air mass. Given the uncertainty, severe
   probabilities will be withheld for now.

   ...Eastern Carolinas...
   While the exact track of the circulation of the coastal low remains
   unclear, model confidence remains high that it will begin to move
   northeastward away from the coast through Sunday. A few
   thunderstorms are possible early in the day before the coastal front
   moves offshore and cooler/drier conditions return. Given the weak
   buoyancy, severe storms are unlikely.

   ..Lyons.. 11/20/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS03 PTSDY3 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
